hits.name: Alex Finn
hits.text:
Gaming is the single biggest opportunity in AI right now

2027 will be an absolute gold rush for anyone who dedicates the time to build a game with AI

Gaming is BY FAR the biggest entertainment industry on Earth

Double the size of the ENTIRE movie, music, and U.S. sports industry combined (NFL, NBA, NHL, MLB) 

Over the past year the economics of gaming has completely collapsed. Despite the industry making over $200 billion a year, it has become completely unaffordable to make good games anymore

The work needed to make a detailed game that keeps up with today's tech is beyond comprehension

This is where AI comes in. AI fixes those economics

AI allows solo devs to build the AAA games of their dreams with very little resources.

The thing is the gaming industry up to this point has completely rejected AI. This won't last much longer though. Disruption is coming and quite literally nothing is going to stop it

The first domino fell today. Asha the CEO of Xbox announced Xbox Labs today. This appears to be one of the first times a major gaming brand is embracing the disruption (for the record Asha has done an INCREDIBLE job being the shepherd of the Xbox brand)

It is so painfully obvious where all of this is going. In the next 12 months every digital game store will be filled with AAA quality, incredibly fun games built entirely with AI by a single developer

The $200 billion flowing through the gaming industry will be redirected from massive studios with thousands of devs to solo developers/small teams embracing the latest tech

The largest entertainment industry in the world will be 100% owned by indie AI developers. Hundreds of billions of dollars up for grabs

And unlike other sectors of software, gaming has built in moats.

One of the last moats in software will be network effects

If I build a community based piece of software that has a million users and you build the exact same piece of software and it has 0 users, everyone will buy my software instead

Gaming encapsulates this perfectly. If you build a banger multiplayer game that has millions of players, even if someone copies you and builds the exact same game, you're going to win because of network effects

This is one of those moments. One of those moments where the future is so obvious and so clear.

AI is about to disrupt a multi hundred billion dollar industry and every penny of that will be up for grabs.

There is absolutely no reason why you can't be one of the people who capitalizes on this

Download Claude Code. Download Codex. Whatever your choice is, just get it. Then start building the game of your dreams

GTA 6 will be a landmark game for many reasons. One of those reasons is it will be the one of the last AAA games from a massive developer studio. That model doesn't work anymore.

The new model is you. A person with an idea and access to the most powerful technology ever created.

Don't screw this opportunity up.

My autonomous Grok Bot business has now made me $1,100

56,000 visitors, 123,000 page views. 2 paying sponsors

I truly believe this is the future of the economy. Everyone having autonomous microbusinesses making $

Here's how I'd set up my own autonomous business if I were you:

1. First you need an idea. Go to your Grok Bot and ask what challenges people in your audience have (it has a new connection with X, so can easily pull posts)

2. Ask for a list of solutions to those challenges

3. Choose a solution, and have it build the idea. It will spin up Cursor agents to build it

4. Ask it to autonomously maintain the site. This will entail:

> monetizing when appropriate
> optimizing SEO
> optimizing for chat bots
> starting and maintaining a newsletter
> watching for feedback on X
> continuously testing and improving the site
> watching for bugs
> updating you on progress
> keeping sponsors happy

This is the exact process I did with my autonomous business https://t.co/S9zybQK14I

If you run this cycle while continuously building your distribution, you can start making money off the effort of your Bot (feel free to share this post with your Grok)

Steer your Grok, build distribution, and watch your autonomous business grow

outsiders.name: ASHA
outsiders.text:
Today we're standing up XBOX LABS (https://t.co/dJSufI1vni). Here is the note that I sent to the team:

Team,
The first video games emerged some 75 years ago. In the time since, there have been booms and busts, but every year there are more great games to play, more devices to play them, and best of all, more people than ever playing. That growth helped make XBOX what it is today, and we've helped shape the industry in return, from bringing hard drives to consoles and online gaming through Xbox Live to Game Pass and cloud gaming, alongside franchises that have brought millions of people together.
In recent weeks, we've seen games rapidly decompiled and rebuilt to run on hardware they were never originally designed to support. Windows PC builds have been translated to run on Apple Silicon or ported to run inside a browser through WebAssembly and WebGPU, the latter now approaching 90% global browser support. Perhaps more surprisingly, we've seen many of the biggest games in the world have been remixed into the source code of another.
These experiments challenge long-held assumptions about our industry: the tether between software and hardware, the boundary between creation and play, and how people discover and experience games. While it is hard to predict the future of gaming, it is easy to see the possibilities in making great games easier to access, giving old games new life and allowing more players to become creators and co-creators. These are unmistakably good outcomes for players, even when (and sometimes because) they challenge our existing business models.
To explore these possibilities, I’ve asked Scott to stand-up XBOX LABS, a small group of game makers, engineers and scientists whose job is to turn emerging ideas into things our players and developers can experience. We'll build in the open, learn from what people do, and measure success by whether more people are playing and creating.
I think XBOX has an important role to play here.  Coding became the first major workload for agents because they can write, run, and test software. Games share many of those same properties, and people spend more than 72 billion hours a year playing XBOX games, roughly five times the estimated time spent writing code worldwide. We've spent 25 years learning how to make great games, and I want our game makers to help shape what these new technologies make possible. As we learn, we’ll share the tools we build with developers across the industry, just as we always have.
Our priorities aren't changing. We remain committed to the 4Cs, to making great games, to our hardware and to being responsible stewards of IP and the communities built around it. LABS gives us a way to explore new technology that is game design led without abandoning the work already underway.
Asha

outsiders.name: Neal Patel
outsiders.text:
You already gave the LLM the answer. So why is it writing it out from scratch?

Introducing a new AI model architecture: Constrained Decoding Models (CDMs)

LLMs were built to write. Most production workloads just need an answer: fast, consistent, and affordable.

CDMs are purpose-built for 1 task each. They read your input once and skip the token-by-token generative loop that makes LLMs slow and expensive.

Not just a decision model, but a family of 3 CDMs live today:

• Classify: define your labels and get back a calibrated probability + reason for each. Used for routing, tagging, and intent detection.
 • Extract: describe the entities in natural language and get back well-formed JSON with confidence scores + citations. Used for web scraping, document processing, and PII redaction.
 • Summarize: pass in long text, images, or PDFs and get back a consistent summary under 1,000 tokens. Used for context compaction, metadata generation, and transcript digests.

Built for production:

• 1M tokens of multimodal (text + image) input, 31x larger than Jev
 • 77.2% on DecisionBench vs Jev's 72%
 • 200x faster, 467x cheaper than frontier LLM APIs
 • $0.05/M input tokens. Output is free (yes, even for summarize)

Live on your favorite platforms today:
 @OpenRouter @vercel_dev @LiteLLM @LangChain  @TrustedRouter @itsArthurAI @useRouterPlus

Get 50M input tokens for free (for the first 50 hours) at link below 👀

virals.angle: AI gaming just got a $200B green light
virals.draft_en:
Xbox just stood up Xbox Labs. 3.9M views on the CEO memo alone.

Asha Sharma's note: AI is decompiling games, porting them to browsers, remixing franchises. Xbox wants to explore that in the open.

Alex Finn called gaming the biggest AI opportunity on Earth. $200B industry. Bigger than movies, music and US sports combined. His bet: solo AI developers own the next wave because multiplayer has network-effect moats.

If you've been waiting for permission to build a game with Claude Code or Codex, this is it. Start one level. Post the clip.
virals.video_tip: 12s: Xbox Labs memo, smash to a solo builder shipping a playable level, store shelf filling with indie AI games, caption permission granted.

virals.draft_en:
Alex Finn's Grok Bot business crossed $1,100. Two sponsors. 56k visitors. He steered. The bot built and sold.

Same window, Pieter priced Nomads data as an API for AI agents at $2.5k–$10k a year. Elon pushed Grok Bot into taxes and music videos.

The pattern: give the agent a job that touches money, then get out of the way.

Pick one niche you know. Give your agent a $1 goal this week. Keep a public log of what it does alone.
virals.inspired_by: @AlexFinn Grok Bot $1,100 (119k + 67k video) + @levelsio Nomads API for agents (68k) + @elonmusk Grok Bot taxes/music (1.5M+)
virals.video_tip: 10s: $0 → $1 → $1,100 counter beside an agent checklist, caption steer once, let it earn.

virals.draft_en:
Hassan got tired of CleanShot and built Matte. Then shipped Gloss, a free open-source reading library for bookmarks and PDFs.

Tony Dinh is ripping out a $600/month newsletter SaaS. swyx ran a real hackathon to clone a $43k/year tool in a weekend.

The age of personal software is here. Rebuild the one tool you hate paying for. Open source it if you can. Post the before and after.
virals.inspired_by: @nutlope Matte (52k) + Gloss launch (9k) + @tdinh_me killing $600 newsletter SaaS (8.4k) + @swyx Kill Your SaaS (15k)
virals.video_tip: 10s: SaaS invoice crossed out, homemade tool boots with your name on it, caption build the seat you were renting.

virals.draft_en:
Theo's week after Muse Wonder and Gemini 4 Argon: it might be months before anything beats Opus 5.5 on price, performance and capability.

He also clapped back at the local-LLM purity test. Eight years of $200 Claude subs vs a sad quantized DeepSeek box. And reminded everyone your $200 plan is a marketing line item next to companies spending $500M a year.

Skip the ranking wars. Run one real task on your daily driver and the new model. Post the side-by-side. That's the only ranking that matters for your work.
virals.inspired_by: @theo 'months until a model beats Opus 5.5' (92k) + $200 Claude vs local DeepSeek (508k) + $500M Anthropic revenue take (188k) + clickhouse Claude/Codex data (101k)
virals.video_tip: 10s: model logos flashing, then one boring real task running on two panes, caption your task is the benchmark.

virals.angle: Stop regenerating answers you already have
virals.draft_en:
Neal Patel asked the obvious question: you already gave the LLM the answer, so why is it writing it from scratch?

Constrained Decoding Models. Classify, Extract, Summarize. 200x faster, 467x cheaper than frontier APIs. Yohei's reaction: this feels different in a good way.

Not every production job needs a generative loop. Some need a fast, consistent answer.

Audit one pipeline this week. If the answer is already in the input, stop regenerating it. Ship the cheaper path.
virals.inspired_by: @neal_k_patel CDMs (1.36M) + @yoheinakajima 'feels different in a good way' (56k) + @levelsio Nomads data-as-API (68k)
virals.video_tip: 8s: token stream rewriting the same JSON, then a skip-straight-to-answer cut, caption stop rewriting what you already know.

virals_narrative: Window Oct 13 ~11:30 CT through Oct 14 ~11:15 CT, minus anything already on yesterday's Muse Wonder / Gemini Argon board. The launch cycle cooled into three money lanes. First, Xbox CEO Asha Sharma stood up Xbox Labs (3.89M★) and Alex Finn called gaming the biggest AI opportunity on Earth — $200B, bigger than movies+music+US sports, with solo AI developers poised to take it (119k★). Second, Finn's Grok Bot microbusiness crossed $1,100 with a full how-to (119k★) and a walkthrough video (67k★), while Elon pushed Grok Bot into taxes and music videos (1.5M+). Third, personal software ate SaaS seats: Hassan shipped Matte (52k★) and launched Gloss (9k), Tony started killing a $600/mo newsletter tool (8.4k), and swyx published Kill Your SaaS results on a real $43k product (15k★). On infrastructure, Pieter priced Nomads data as an agent API (68k★) and Neal Patel's Constrained Decoding Models (1.36M★) asked why LLMs rewrite answers already in context — Yohei felt it (56k★). Theo, still posting as @theo not @t3dotgg, said it may be months before anything beats Opus 5.5 (92k★) and clapped the local-LLM purity test (508k★). The meta: give your agent a job that earns, rebuild the tool you hate renting, and if you're building games, the green light just turned on.

Autonomous microbusinesses that earn: @AlexFinn Grok Bot at $1,100 with a how-to (119k★) plus the step-by-step video (67k★); @elonmusk pushing Grok Bot into taxes (1.59M★) and music videos (1.39M★)

Personal software replaces seats: @nutlope ships Matte after CleanShot fatigue (52k★) and launches Gloss open-source (9k); @tdinh_me ripping out a $600/mo newsletter SaaS (8.4k); @swyx Kill Your SaaS hackathon on a real $43k tool (15k★)

Data and APIs for agents: @levelsio Nomads paid API $2.5k–$10k/yr built for AI agents (68k★); @neal_k_patel Constrained Decoding Models 200x faster / 467x cheaper (1.36M★) with @yoheinakajima 'feels different' (56k★)

Opus still the daily driver: @theo 'months until a model beats Opus 5.5' (92k★), $200 Claude vs local DeepSeek clapback (508k★), $500M Anthropic enterprise reality (188k★), near-complete move from Codex to Claude (55k★)
AI is already normal outside tech: @levelsio 'regular people use AI in advanced ways' (51k★) quoting an airport lounge attendant on Claude Code / Opus 5.5 (@OnurAppDev 49k★)
Human beats between launches: @lexfridman Taiwan with Jensen (457k★) quote-boosted by Pieter (54k★); Pieter Warsaw tips (41k★) and tram posts; Ben Tossell's twins talking to computers (5.8k)
Codegen volume panic: @jimstewartson on Anthropic's 30k code changes/day (502k★) and Theo's clapback that a 2,000-person company merging under 30 PRs/day is the absurd take (104k★)
